title: Install and maintain Platter
summary: Install and maintain Platter under coordinated maintenance. Import schema-one runtime files into SQLite while preserving packet and delivery history.
use_when: The user wants Platter installed, replaced, inspected or maintained.
The caller needs prerequisite readiness, admission holds, draining or supported installed-release verification.
An operator must preserve a separately managed Clockwork daily binding while upgrading its pinned Platter runner.
do_not_use_when: The requested outcome is packet preparation, a test email, job discovery, profile editing or scheduled delivery.
The caller expects arbitrary direct rollback, a schema reset or implicit installation of dependencies.
outcome: A verified installation with matching Platter command and provider, supported maintenance state, or a local readiness result. Stored domain history remains intact.

interfaces.label: Install the committed candidate under maintenance
Validate supported state and take deployment backup
Print the selected release daily failure policy without activation

effects: Coordinated installation publishes exact runtime/installer/provider bytes and owned selectors; it creates no domain work or schedule.
Owner-keyed SQLite holds fence the canonical library. A database-file activity lock serializes commands, while predecessor gate/runner locks are observed through cutover.
An explicit transaction imports legacy records and files into schema two, writes a complete schema-two backup, then removes only the hashed legacy files on its retained cleanup manifest.
Readiness checks validate state and executable/runtime prerequisites without preparing jobs, rendering PDFs or sending email.
authority: Platter owns domain compatibility, admission, drain policy, retained state and success. Nucleus owns execution state and cancellation.
Cell coordinates selected product installation and maintenance; the shared installer owns artifact integrity, owned selectors, writer locks and file compensation.
Catalog presence, a successful build or stored delivery time grants no installation, send, recurring-delivery or dependency-upgrade authority.
success: Installation succeeds only after exact candidate selection, state and local prerequisites are verified while held and run-owned maintenance is released.
Inspection and doctor report the installation, configuration and dependency readiness checks they perform.
failure_and_recovery: Foreign selectors, altered releases, ambiguous state roots, unsupported schemas, missing legacy content and conflicting holds stop the operation.
Schema migration preserves exact input and delivery identities. Failure before import commit leaves schema one; failure afterward retains schema two plus originals and cleanup recovery metadata.

Older binaries cannot operate schema two. A binary-only rollback is unsafe; recovery needs a compatible candidate or an explicitly selected complete predecessor database/files backup and matching binary.
Uncertain apply or recovery remains held. No automatic model retry, domain reset or direct installer rollback is supported.

The daily runner stops at the first preparation error before another candidate or email starts. Declined opportunities, unavailable/stale ready-packet deferrals and an empty ready pool remain expected domain outcomes. Clockwork owns durable halt-until-approved enforcement, incident notification and explicit continuation; deployment and binding changes preserve halts and do not authorize a retry or uncertain resend.
privacy: Private state and backup files contain career history, original resume and packet/send metadata. They remain separate from immutable public installation material and source control.

Installation manifests retain executable/provider identity and local paths, never private resume bodies or provider keys. Model and email disclosures belong only to separately authorized runtime operations.
does_not_authorize: Preparing packets, sending email, collecting jobs, consuming Cast API-key budgets or submitting replacement Nucleus work.
Installing or enabling a daily schedule, changing provider credentials/billing or upgrading unselected dependencies.
Resetting sent flags, deleting retained artifacts, changing fixed resume content or bypassing an unresolved maintenance hold.

consumers.statement: The current user and the Cell coordinator may operate the supported installation, readiness and maintenance interfaces.

preconditions.statement: Coordinated deployment requires committed local main source, a verified candidate, owned current-user paths and compatible maintenance interfaces throughout the Nucleus requester closure. Required runtime commands, Email attachment support and local renderer tooling must be available. When selected together, Cast, CRM, Email and Nucleus are applied before Platter; ordering declarations do not implicitly select their upgrades.
A state backup requires the exact deployment hold and quiescence. Unsupported state or ambiguous default roots stop installation; initialization is a separate explicit runtime operation.

inputs.statement: Cell selects exact committed source and supplies sealed adapter JSON. migrate requires the sole CELL_DEPLOYMENT_RUN_ID hold, drained requester work and an absolute backup path. Coordinated Platter backups use the canonical runtime root/backups directory. Renderer overrides remain absolute.

outputs.statement: Coherent immutable installation selectors and integrity manifests, maintenance/readiness outcomes, or a self-contained schema-two SQLite backup with a resumable legacy cleanup manifest.

data_semantics.statement: Database schema 2 holds all durable Platter content, explicit job eligibility and maintenance state. A consistent SQLite backup contains the complete retained library. Nucleus history and credentials remain separately owned.

identity_and_units.statement: Existing packet IDs become run IDs. Retained job-packets requester identities, Nucleus requests, edition keys, frozen bytes, attachment names/order and receipts remain exact. Hold ownership is durable and never expires automatically.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Maintenance checks live admissions and every page of matching nonterminal Nucleus jobs for both requester identities. Doctor validates existing local state, Cast/CRM/Email executable identity, Email attachment flag, renderer tools and compatible Nucleus health without exercising domain operations. It does not prove initialized Cast or CRM libraries or read their domain contents.
Installation inspection reports selected releases and stored configuration; strict doctor checks the documented runtime dependencies.

access.statement: Installed commands/provider retain their owned selectors under Application Support and ~/.local/bin. Runtime state is the single canonical ~/.local/share/platter root or a sole predecessor job-packets root. Independent --state-dir libraries are unsupported. Owner holds reside in SQLite; predecessor gate files are retired after drained release.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Requester holds and draining precede Nucleus maintenance; verification precedes run-owned release and Nucleus is released last. Live command admission uses the database file itself. Existing legacy gate/runner activity is respected during transition.

Schema-one import is transactional. A complete schema-two backup precedes hashed legacy-file cleanup. Interrupted backup or cleanup is resumable without regenerating packets, resending or resetting identities.

Installation does not update an operator-managed platter/daily binding. Capture and disable it for scheduled-runner cutover, deploy and verify Platter through Cell, then register the exact new runner definition and restore the prior enabled state under drained Platter maintenance. Preserve prior binding and verified release evidence for recovery.

operational_limits.statement: No installation operation prepares packets, sends email, initializes a resume or enables a schedule. Renderer scratch remains under the runtime root; program installations and Nucleus state remain separate.
No installation latency, arbitrary incompatible rollback, future support interval or deprecation window is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Installation uses cell-install-v2, private schema two, preparation contract three and installation contract two. Schema one requires the explicit import. Older binaries cannot read schema two. Recovery requires a compatible candidate or a complete predecessor backup with its matching binary.

reliances.statement: Nucleus supplies compatible execution health and cancellation of matching orphaned jobs.
Runtime prerequisite probes rely on supported Cast and CRM commands and Email attachment support; unselected installations are not upgraded implicitly.

Cell deployment source and cell-install transactions supply exact committed candidate preparation, coordinator sequencing, artifact integrity and file compensation. Their source operational manual remains the authority; this entry does not claim an independent installed Cell capability contract.
Resume readiness depends on Tectonic, Python 3 with pypdf, and the original template packages/fonts.

The product-owned schema-two definition declares halt-until-approved. Clockwork owns activation, durable failure admission, incident email and explicit continuation; Platter owns expected readiness outcomes, date selection and preserved preparation/delivery recovery.
